findings.problem: The owned boundary precedes SDK callTool, but the pinned SDK compiles its output schema and awaits buildSendOptions before its native request/send. The owned transport send is not wrapped with a fresh absolute-clock/abort check.
findings.staticCounterexample: At the last owned call boundary elapsed work is below15000ms and signal is not aborted. A schema-compilation step or earlier queued microtask consumes the remaining absolute budget. The SDK continuation runs before the timers phase, so the work timer is still unexecuted and its signal check remains false. It installs a relative timer and calls transport.send, writing tools/call after the absolute work deadline. The outer post-call boundary can refuse later but cannot undo dispatch.
findings.qualification: Source-only event ordering; no timing probe, fixture execution or assertion of an observed remote deadline overrun. This corroborates the author requested tightening; no future fix accepted.
findings.requiredNarrowCorrection: Reobserve the original absolute work clock plus abort/closed/first-failure at the actual owned transport send boundary after SDK compilation/queued continuations and before delegating the write. Keep no new child/call/retry and memoized one-close. Preserve the SDK promise-returning send error contract, including cancellation notification callers. Add bounded native/injected positive and zero-send deadline/abort controls; keep actual SDK entries at most3.

findings.problem: actualEntry replaces process.stdout.write and unconditionally captures every chunk during the awaited SDK entry; it does not delegate the Node test runner/report/IPC writes. writes===1 and JSON parsing then treat those unrelated chunks as client terminal output, and the original runner records can be swallowed.
findings.staticCounterexample: A native reporter/IPC chunk arrives while actualEntry awaits the SDK child. The replacement increments writes, appends the chunk, calls its callback and returns true without priorWrite. The correct terminal result produces a second write; writes===1 fails and the reporter chunk was never emitted. Earlier asynchronous case outcomes can therefore be absent from the retained original without proving those cases passed.
